narrative: 把画面当作一张关于“谁拥有空间”的图式来对待。三分法是一种默认选择，而不是一条法则。
把一张脸放在一个有分量的交叉点上，就等于把更大的那块矩形让给了目光、天气，或威胁。头部后方的那条空白带是剩余空间，而不是装饰。
当这场戏需要一座正式的祭坛、一个陷阱，或一个关于秩序的笑话时，这就不是对的工具。正中央的仪式感、短边构图式的恐慌，以及海报式的对称，都是刻意打破这套网格的例子。
如果你把三分法用在每一个特写上，这套图式就会失去意义。一个只听懂“均衡构图”这一指令的模型，只会把脸居中，把天空对半分。
要明确指出哪个交叉点承载着眼睛，哪个三分线承载着地平线。
how: 在监视器上打开3x3的辅助网格。把眼睛、头部，或一个地标放在某个交叉点上，而不是放在某个格子的正中央。
除非侧滚本身就是重点，否则要保持摄影机水平。35mm到50mm的焦段能让这套网格保持诚实。
超广角镜头会把外侧的三分之一区域拉伸成卡通般的角落，长焦镜头则会把它们压缩成堆叠的条带。
提示词：Rule-of-thirds placement of [Subject] on a power intersection, horizon on a third, breathing room in the look direction.
when: 用它拍摄一次风景中的行走、一次目光望向画外的单人镜头，或一个必须显得“有内容”却又不至于变成祭坛的建立镜头广角。不要把它当成一种宗教信条，用在每一个特写、字幕卡，或仪式性的活人画上。
vs: 0.618黄金比例（Golden Ratio）用的是大约38%和62%的分割方式，而不是精确的三分之一。前导空间（Lead Room）是三分法通常为目光或行走所留出的水平空气。
中心构图（Centered Composition）拒绝这种偏移，把主体放在轴线上。短边构图（Short Siding）则是相反的图式：视线被压向它所面对的边缘。
examples_film: 经典好莱坞覆盖镜头把三分法当作单人镜头和风景镜头的默认图式；《阿拉伯的劳伦斯》（Lawrence of Arabia）把地平线安置在三分线上，让沙漠占据画面其余的部分。
《天堂之日》（Days of Heaven）对草原和天空也如法炮制；《血色将至》（There Will Be Blood）常常把人物偏移安置，让土地的分量压过人物本身。
这些都是语法，而不是要照搬的画面。
mistakes: 最常见的误用是一张正中央的肖像，却假装成三分法构图。破绽是一张位于光学轴线上的脸，两只耳朵旁边的天空和剩余空间都完全相等。
修正方法：把眼睛滑动到一个交叉点上，把更大的区域留给目光方向，或者干脆承认你想要的其实是正中取景（Central Framing），转而拍摄那种构图。

faq.q: 电影中的三分法（Rule of Thirds）是什么？
faq.a: 它是叠加在画面上的一套3x3网格。重要的质量块位于网格线上或四个交叉点上，使画面默认呈现偏移状态。更大的剩余区域通常属于目光、土地，或威胁。

faq.q: 三分法（Rule of Thirds）与黄金比例（Golden Ratio）有何区别？
faq.a: 三分法在33%处分割。黄金比例或phi网格则更接近38%和62%处分割，偏移幅度略微更紧凑，有时被描述为一条螺旋线。两者都拒绝正中央的构图。三分法是片场上更快捷的默认选择，phi比例则是一种更为低调的比例主张。

faq.q: 什么时候该用三分法（Rule of Thirds）？
faq.a: 当一个人物或地平线应当与一片他们并未占据的更大区域共享画面时使用它：一次行走、一次望向画外的目光、一个风景单人镜头。当这场戏是一场仪式、一个陷阱，或一张需要轴线感的海报时，就不要使用它。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写三分法（Rule of Thirds）的提示词？
faq.a: 指明交叉点和地平线的位置。示例：Rule-of-thirds placement of [Subject] on a power intersection, horizon on a third, breathing room in the look direction。说明是偏左还是偏右。如果你只写“均衡构图”，模型会把脸居中处理。

narrative: Treat the frame as a diagram of who owns space. Thirds is a default, not a law.
A face on a power intersection hands the bigger rectangle to the look, the weather, or the threat. The strip behind the head is leftover, not decoration.
It is the wrong tool when the beat needs a formal altar, a trap, or a joke about order. Dead-center ritual, short-sided panic, and poster symmetry all break the grid on purpose.
If you apply thirds to every close-up, the diagram stops meaning anything. A model that hears only balanced composition will center the face and split the sky in half.
Name which intersection holds the eyes and which third holds the horizon.
how: Turn on the 3x3 overlay on the monitor. Place eyes, a head, or a landmark on an intersection, not in the dead middle of a cell.
Keep the camera level unless a roll is the point. A 35mm to 50mm keeps the grid honest.
Ultra-wide glass stretches the outer thirds into cartoon corners. Telephoto compresses them into stacked bands.
Prompt: Rule-of-thirds placement of [Subject] on a power intersection, horizon on a third, breathing room in the look direction.
when: Use it on a landscape walk, a single looking off, or an establishing wide that must feel occupied without becoming an altar. Do not treat it as a religion on every close-up, title card, or ritual tableau.
vs: 618 instead of one-third. Lead Room is the horizontal air that thirds usually create for a look or a walk.
Centered Composition refuses the offset and puts the subject on the axis. Short Siding is the opposite diagram: the look is crushed against the edge it faces.
examples_film: Classical coverage treats thirds as the default diagram for singles and landscapes. Lawrence of Arabia parks horizons on a third so desert owns the rest of the frame.
Days of Heaven does the same with prairie and sky. There Will Be Blood often offsets a figure so land outweighs the person.
These are grammar, not frames to copy.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is dead-center portrait posing as thirds. The tell is a face on the optical axis with equal sky and equal leftover on both ears.
The fix is to slide the eyes to an intersection and give the look the larger field, or admit you wanted Central Framing and shoot that instead.

faq.q: What is rule of thirds in film?
faq.a: It is a 3x3 grid overlaid on the frame. Important masses sit on the lines or at the four intersections so the picture is offset by default. The larger remaining field usually belongs to the look, the land, or the threat.

faq.q: Rule of Thirds vs Golden Ratio
faq.a: Thirds splits at 33 percent. A golden-ratio or phi grid splits nearer 38 and 62 percent, a slightly tighter offset, sometimes described as a spiral. Both refuse dead center. Thirds is the faster default on a set. Phi is a quieter proportional claim.

faq.q: When should I use rule of thirds?
faq.a: Use it when a figure or horizon should share the frame with a larger field they do not occupy. A walk, a look off, a landscape single. Skip it when the scene is a ritual, a trap, or a poster that needs the axis.

faq.q: How do I prompt rule of thirds for AI image or video?
faq.a: Name the intersection and the horizon line. Example: Rule-of-thirds placement of [Subject] on a power intersection, horizon on a third, breathing room in the look direction. Say left or right. If you only write balanced, the model will center the face.
